I'm weighing how to label the candidate mentions in this abstract: the specific disease "Autosomal dominant neurohypophyseal diabetes insipidus" looks like a Specific Disease, while the bare "diabetes insipidus" reads as a Disease Class. For "This disorder," I'm leaning toward no annotation, since it's a pronoun referring back to that specific disease and "disorder" is too general to count as a named mention.

Now I'm settling on the labels for the remaining mentions: "diabetes insipidus" in "diabetes insipidus of varying severity" is a general class, so it's a Disease Class. The full "autosomal dominant neurohypophyseal diabetes insipidus" appears again and still counts as a Specific Disease.

Now I'm marking the familial diabetes insipidus mention as a Disease Class, since it covers several specific forms, and the bare "disorder" pronoun stays unannotated. The last specific-disease mention is a repeat, so it gets the same label.

content.text: {"decisions":[{"id":1,"entity":"SpecificDisease","rationale":"'Autosomal dominant neurohypophyseal diabetes insipidus' names one specific form of diabetes insipidus with its own definition (inheritance pattern and site of defect), so it is a Specific Disease rather than a class.","guideline_section":"What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate 5 (minimum necessary span)"},{"id":2,"entity":"DiseaseClass","rationale":"'diabetes insipidus' used generically as a familial form of diabetes insipidus refers to a family of multiple specific diseases (central, nephrogenic, etc.), so it is a Disease Class.","guideline_section":"What to Annotate 1 (Disease Class)"},{"id":3,"entity":"NONE","rationale":"'This disorder' is a pronominal reference using the general term 'disorder', which is excluded as a general term and is not a disease name in its own right.","guideline_section":"What NOT to Annotate 4 (general terms such as 'disease' and 'syndrome' are excluded)"},{"id":4,"entity":"DiseaseClass","rationale":"'diabetes insipidus of varying severity' refers to diabetes insipidus in general, a category covering several specific diseases, so it is a Disease Class.","guideline_section":"What to Annotate 1 (Disease Class)"},{"id":5,"entity":"SpecificDisease","rationale":"This is a duplicate mention of the same specific form of diabetes insipidus as candidate 1 and is annotated separately as its own occurrence.","guideline_section":"What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); What to Annotate 4 (duplicate mentions)"}]}
